note: Batch was routed here as figure-bearing, but pages 829-840 contain NO general-format / syntax-skeleton diagrams. Content is clause 15.3 (date/time format arguments), 15.4 (returned values), 15.5 (date/time conversion forms), 15.6 (Summary of functions) plus the first four pages of Table 21, Table of functions. The choice-indicator (5.2.6.4 vertical-bar) defect class therefore has no instances on these pages. Prose and all Table 21 cells were compared verbatim and are faithful; the only defects found are heading-level (nesting) errors.

findings.pdf_says: 15.3   Arguments  ...  15.3.1   Format arguments to international date and time functions  /  15.3.1.1   General
findings.markdown_says: line 33363: `### 15.3 Arguments`  ...  line 33438: `## 15.3.1 Format arguments to international date and time functions`  /  line 33440: `### 15.3.1.1 General`
findings.why_it_matters: The heading hierarchy is inverted: the child 15.3.1 is emitted at markdown level 2 while its parent 15.3 is at level 3, and the grandchild 15.3.1.1 is emitted at the same level 3 as 15.3. Any TOC or section-tree built from the markdown headings detaches 15.3.1 from 15.3 and makes 15.3.1.1 a sibling of 15.3. Elsewhere in clause 15 the convention is `## 15.x` / `### 15.x.y` (e.g. `## 15.4 Returned values` / `### 15.5.1 General`).
findings.suggested_repair: Promote `### 15.3 Arguments` to `## 15.3 Arguments` and demote `## 15.3.1 ...` to `### 15.3.1 ...`, then rebase the whole 15.3 subtree so 15.3.1.n is `####`; or, matching the dominant file convention, keep 15.3 at `##`, 15.3.1 at `###`, 15.3.1.n at `####`.

findings.pdf_says: 15.3.1.5   Permissible values for data associated with ordinal date formats / 15.3.1.6   Week date formats / 15.3.1.7   Permissible values for data associated with week date formats  — all printed at the same rank as 15.3.1.1 through 15.3.1.4 on page 829
findings.markdown_says: `## 15.3.1.5 Permissible values for data associated with ordinal date formats`, `## 15.3.1.6 Week date formats`, `## 15.3.1.7 Permissible values for data associated with week date formats` (all level 2), whereas their siblings on page 829 are `### 15.3.1.1 General`, `### 15.3.1.2 Calendar date formats`, `### 15.3.1.3 ...`, `### 15.3.1.4 Ordinal date formats` (level 3)
findings.why_it_matters: Sibling subsections of the same parent 15.3.1 are transcribed at two different markdown levels. 15.3.1.5, .6 and .7 render as peers of 15.3.1 itself rather than as its children, so a generated section tree loses the parent-child relationship for exactly the subsections that carry the permissible-value ranges for ordinal and week dates.
findings.suggested_repair: Change the three headings from `##` to `###` so they match 15.3.1.1-15.3.1.4.

findings.pdf_says: 15.3.3.3   Permissible values for data associated with common time formats / 15.3.3.4   Local time formats / 15.3.3.5   UTC time formats / 15.3.3.6   Offset time formats / 15.3.3.6.1   Offset subformats
findings.markdown_says: `## 15.3.3.3 ...`, `## 15.3.3.4 Local time formats`, `## 15.3.3.5 UTC time formats`, `## 15.3.3.6 Offset time formats`, `## 15.3.3.6.1 Offset subformats` (all level 2), whereas siblings `### 15.3.3.1 Common time formats with integer seconds representation` and `### 15.3.3.2 Common time formats with fractional seconds representation` (page 831) and `### 15.3.3.6.2 Permissible values for data associated with offset time formats` (page 833) are level 3
findings.why_it_matters: Same defect as page 830 and additionally one level deeper: 15.3.3.6.1 is emitted at level 2 while its own sibling 15.3.3.6.2 is at level 3, so the two halves of the offset-subformat specification end up at different depths and 15.3.3.6.1 detaches from 15.3.3.6.

findings.pdf_says: 15.4   Returned values  ...  15.4.1   Numeric and integer functions
findings.markdown_says: `## 15.4 Returned values` immediately followed by `## 15.4.1 Numeric and integer functions` — both level 2
findings.why_it_matters: 15.4.1 is emitted at the same markdown level as its parent 15.4, so it renders as a peer clause rather than a subclause. The parallel construction two clauses later is transcribed correctly (`## 15.5 Date and time conversion functions` / `### 15.5.1 General`), which shows the intended convention.
findings.suggested_repair: Change `## 15.4.1 Numeric and integer functions` to `### 15.4.1 Numeric and integer functions`.

findings.pdf_says: 15.5.3   Standard date form / 15.5.4   Julian date form / 15.5.5   Standard numeric time form
findings.markdown_says: `## 15.5.3 Standard date form`, `## 15.5.4 Julian date form`, `## 15.5.5 Standard numeric time form` (level 2), whereas their siblings on page 835 are `### 15.5.1 General` and `### 15.5.2 Integer date form` (level 3)
findings.why_it_matters: Sibling subclauses of 15.5 are split across two markdown levels, so 15.5.3 through 15.5.5 render as peers of 15.5 and of 15.6 rather than as children of 15.5. These are the clauses that define standard date form, Julian date form and standard numeric time form — heavily cross-referenced by the intrinsic-function definitions.
findings.suggested_repair: Change the three headings from `##` to `###` so they match 15.5.1 and 15.5.2.
